correctness.rationale: A permitted face meets at most two blocks and, if it meets two, has at most one vertex in one of them. For pair i<j, the two joins with one full simplex are contractible and intersect in the connected graph K_{a_i,a_j}. The homotopy pushout along simplicial cofibrations is its suspension, a wedge of (a_i-1)(a_j-1) two-spheres (contractible for a singleton block). Distinct pair spaces meet only in common block simplices. Collapsing those contractible vertex spaces separately preserves homotopy type; equivalently use the double mapping cylinder at each edge of K_r. After a spanning tree connects the components, each remaining edge-space attachment contributes one circle, while every attachment retains its pair-space sphere summands. For integral naturality set A equal to the disjoint union of the block simplices. H_2(X) maps isomorphically to H_2(X,A), whose relative chains split by block pairs, and hence to the sum of the pair H_2 groups. In each pair the natural Mayer–Vietoris map gives the integral cycle lattice of the bipartite graph: since oriented edges run from i to j, its integral cycles are exactly matrices with all row and column sums zero, the tensor of the two augmentation kernels. The affine map collapsing blocks to their index vertices induces an isomorphism on H_1: H_1(X,A) is one free copy of Z per pair, with connecting map the usual incidence matrix. This also proves trivial within-block action on H_1. In RESULT.md line 40, 'four-simplex' should read 'tetrahedron (3-simplex)'; the four-element forbidden set and its allowed triangular boundary are unambiguous, so this does not affect the claim. The uploaded field checker was inspected, not run; the all-size integral result follows from the proof, not the field comparisons.
residual_risks: This does not assert a homotopy splitting equivariant under any permutations; the module action is only under within-block permutations.

evidence: Selvaraja's chordal bound gives 3-collapsibility at tolerance one (hence vanishing in degrees at least three), without computing the lower-degree ranks or modules. broader_coverage.reasoning: In the shared subclass the exact wedge is covered, not merely bounded. In the full-simplex problem, a block of size at least three and a vertex of a second block give a permissible four-element face, whereas the one-dimensional-input tolerance complex has none; the two-body decomposition is extra information, not a direct application to the one-dimensional skeleton.

value.rationale: For a natural family of disconnected chordal clique complexes the result gives an all-size integral answer, not a recomputation of the old two-block sphere. It identifies exactly when both homology degrees occur and gives the actual integral action in degree two, useful for symmetry and quotient calculations not provided by a collapsibility bound or ordinary Betti numbers.
